description: NFS shares mounted into a consumer guest (ADR-029): a TAPPaaS export on a cluster node, a share on a registered, unmanaged server, or an unmodelled server's path.
_note: The consumer's side only. The node's own exports are the module-tier `nfs` object (pvehost/fields.json), converged by pvehost/update.sh; this service checks a consumer's mounts against them (the two-key check), has the node build a declared export it names (D11), and writes the mounts into the guest. The `nfs` object's DEFINITION lives in the module tier (pvehost/fields.json) because registered NFS servers carry it too; its change semantics are here, with the service that converges it, as backup:filesystem does for `backup`.

nfs.changeNote: Converged by the node's own update (pvehost/update.sh → nfs_node_reconcile): exports are created, re-quota'd, re-granted and unshared live; nothing reboots. name, pool and an allocated owner are immutable in substance — a rename or a pool move is a data migration and is not attempted; the reconcile treats the old dataset as an orphan and keeps it.

mounts.description: The NFS shares this guest mounts (ADR-029 D3). Each entry: {path, share, access?, required?}. share is <instance>:<name> for a share declared on a module instance, or <host>:/<path> for an unmodelled server.

path.description: Absolute directory in the guest. Not /, /etc, /nix, /var, /usr, /boot or a system path.

share.description: <instance>:<name> (a share on a module instance — the grant is checked) or <host>:/<path> (an unmodelled server).

access.description: What the consumer asks for. Must not exceed the export's grant.

required.description: false: nofail + automount — the guest boots and the app starts without the share. true: the mount is required at boot.

mounts.changeNote: The mounts are reconciled whole: update-service.sh rewrites the guest's generated mount list (NixOS fragment, applied by the rebuild the update runs; Debian fstab block, applied at once). Adding or removing a mount remounts; nothing reboots and no share data is touched.
